subject: Biology SL
question: Answer all parts using the shared DNA-sequence data.

stimulus.title: Differences in a homologous DNA sequence
stimulus.description: Researchers compared the same 1200-base DNA region in four related species. The number of nucleotide differences for selected species pairs is shown.
stimulus.note: The same aligned DNA region and comparison method were used for every pair.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.question: Identify the pair of species that is most closely related according to the data.
markscheme: P and Q, because they have the fewest nucleotide differences (18).
markschemeJa: PとQ。ヌクレオチドの違いが18と最も少ないため。

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.question: Calculate the percentage of bases that differ between species P and Q. Give your answer to two significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain how DNA-sequence differences can be used to infer evolutionary relationships.
markscheme: Mutations cause homologous DNA sequences to accumulate differences over evolutionary time.
Fewer sequence differences generally indicate a more recent common ancestor, provided homologous regions are compared consistently.
markschemeJa: 突然変異によって相同DNA配列には進化の時間とともに違いが蓄積する。
同じ相同領域を一貫した方法で比較する場合、配列差が少ないほど一般により最近の共通祖先をもつと推定できる。
parts.modelAnswer: Mutations accumulate in DNA through evolutionary time. When the same homologous region is compared, species with fewer sequence differences are generally inferred to share a more recent common ancestor.
parts.modelAnswerJa: DNAには進化の時間とともに突然変異による違いが蓄積します。同じ相同領域を比較した場合、配列差が少ない種どうしほど一般により最近の共通祖先をもつと推定できます。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Evaluate one limitation of using this DNA region alone to decide the evolutionary relationships among the four species.
markscheme: One short DNA region may not represent evolutionary history across the whole genome, so additional independent sequences would strengthen the inference.
Molecular evidence should ideally be considered with other evidence such as morphology, fossils or reproductive evidence before drawing a strong conclusion.
markschemeJa: 1つの短いDNA領域だけではゲノム全体の進化史を代表しない可能性があるため、独立した複数の配列を調べると推論が強くなる。
強い結論には、分子証拠を形態、化石、生殖に関する証拠など他の証拠と合わせて考えることが望ましい。
parts.modelAnswer: This sequence is only one small part of the genome, so its pattern may not fully represent the species' evolutionary history. Comparing additional independent DNA regions and other biological evidence would make the conclusion more reliable.
parts.modelAnswerJa: この配列はゲノムのごく一部なので、そのパターンだけでは種全体の進化史を十分に表さない可能性があります。複数の独立したDNA領域や他の生物学的証拠も比較すると結論の信頼性が高まります。

subject: Biology SL
question: Answer all parts using the shared osmosis investigation.

stimulus.title: Change in potato-cylinder mass in sucrose solutions
stimulus.description: Equal-sized potato cylinders were placed in sucrose solutions for 60 minutes. Mean percentage change in mass was calculated from four cylinders at each concentration.
stimulus.note: Positive values indicate a gain in mass; negative values indicate a loss in mass.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Estimate the sucrose concentration at which there would be no net change in potato mass.
markscheme: Approximately 0.47 mol dm⁻³; accept a reasonable estimate between about 0.46 and 0.48 mol dm⁻³.
markschemeJa: 約0.47 mol dm⁻³。およそ0.46〜0.48 mol dm⁻³の妥当な推定を可とする。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain why the potato cylinders gain mass in dilute sucrose solutions but lose mass in concentrated sucrose solutions.
markscheme: Water moves by osmosis across partially permeable cell membranes from higher water potential to lower water potential.
Dilute external solutions have higher water potential than the potato cells so water enters, whereas concentrated sucrose solutions have lower water potential so water leaves.
markschemeJa: 水は部分透過性膜を通って、水ポテンシャルの高い側から低い側へ浸透で移動する。
薄い外液では細胞より水ポテンシャルが高いため水が入り、濃いスクロース溶液では外液の水ポテンシャルが低いため水が出る。
parts.modelAnswer: Water moves by osmosis from higher to lower water potential. In dilute sucrose solutions water enters the potato cells, increasing mass, while in concentrated solutions water leaves the cells, decreasing mass.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 水は水ポテンシャルの高い側から低い側へ浸透します。薄いスクロース溶液では水が細胞内へ入り質量が増え、濃い溶液では水が細胞外へ出て質量が減ります。

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.question: Suggest two variables, other than sucrose concentration, that should be controlled in this investigation.
markscheme: Control the initial size or mass / surface area of the potato cylinders.
Control a relevant condition such as immersion time, temperature, potato tissue source or total solution volume.
markschemeJa: ジャガイモ円柱の初期サイズ・質量・表面積をそろえる。
浸漬時間、温度、ジャガイモ組織の由来、溶液量など適切な条件を一定にする。
parts.modelAnswer: The cylinders should have the same initial size or mass, and conditions such as immersion time and temperature should be kept constant.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 円柱の初期サイズや質量をそろえ、浸漬時間や温度などの条件を一定にします。

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.question: Explain how the reliability of the estimated concentration for no net mass change could be improved.
markscheme: Use more replicate cylinders at each concentration and calculate a mean to reduce the influence of random variation.
Test additional sucrose concentrations close to the zero-change point to reduce the interval over which the estimate must be interpolated.
markschemeJa: 各濃度で反復数を増やして平均を求め、偶然のばらつきの影響を小さくする。
質量変化0付近でより細かい濃度間隔を追加し、補間する範囲を狭くする。
parts.modelAnswer: More replicate cylinders should be used at each concentration and a mean calculated. Additional concentrations around 0.47 mol dm⁻³ would also allow a more precise estimate of the zero-change point.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 各濃度の反復数を増やして平均を求め、さらに0.47 mol dm⁻³付近を細かい濃度間隔で測定すると、質量変化0となる点をより正確に推定できます。

subject: Biology SL
question: Answer all parts using the shared enzyme-rate data.

stimulus.title: Effect of substrate concentration on enzyme reaction rate
stimulus.description: Reaction rate was measured at different substrate concentrations while enzyme concentration, pH and temperature were kept constant.
stimulus.note: Each plotted value is the mean of three repeated measurements.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Describe the relationship between substrate concentration and reaction rate.
markscheme: Reaction rate increases as substrate concentration increases, especially at lower substrate concentrations.
The increase becomes progressively smaller and the rate approaches a plateau of about 6.0 arbitrary units min⁻¹ at high substrate concentration.
markschemeJa: 基質濃度が増えると反応速度は上昇し、特に低濃度で増加が大きい。
高濃度になるにつれて増加幅は小さくなり、約6.0 arbitrary units min⁻¹付近で頭打ちに近づく。
parts.modelAnswer: Reaction rate rises with substrate concentration at first, but the increase becomes smaller at higher concentrations and the rate approaches a plateau near 6.0 units min⁻¹.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 基質濃度が上がると最初は反応速度が大きく増えますが、高濃度では増加幅が小さくなり、約6.0 units min⁻¹付近で頭打ちになります。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain the plateau in reaction rate at high substrate concentration.
markscheme: At high substrate concentration, most enzyme active sites are occupied for much of the time.
Enzyme concentration becomes limiting, so adding more substrate produces little further increase in the maximum reaction rate.
markschemeJa: 高い基質濃度では、多くの酵素の活性部位がほとんどの時間で基質に占有される。
酵素濃度が制限要因となるため、基質をさらに増やしても最大反応速度はほとんど上がらない。
parts.modelAnswer: At high substrate concentration, enzyme active sites are close to saturation. The amount of enzyme then limits the maximum rate, so extra substrate has little effect.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 高い基質濃度では酵素の活性部位がほぼ飽和し、酵素量そのものが最大速度を制限するため、基質を増やしてもほとんど速度が上がりません。

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.question: Predict the effect of doubling enzyme concentration while keeping a high substrate concentration and other conditions unchanged.
markscheme: The maximum reaction rate would be expected to increase because more active sites would be available, provided substrate remains abundant.
markschemeJa: 基質が十分にあるなら、利用可能な活性部位が増えるため最大反応速度は上昇すると予測される。
parts.modelAnswer: The maximum rate should increase because more enzyme active sites would be available.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 利用可能な酵素の活性部位が増えるため、最大反応速度は上昇すると予測されます。

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.question: Evaluate the reliability of the plotted values and suggest one further improvement.
markscheme: Using three repeated measurements and plotting a mean reduces the influence of a single random measurement and improves reliability.
Reliability could be assessed or improved further by increasing the number of repeats and showing variation such as a range, standard deviation or error bars.
markschemeJa: 3回の反復測定から平均を示すことで、1回の偶然の測定値の影響を小さくし信頼性を高めている。
反復数をさらに増やし、range、標準偏差、error barなどばらつきも示すと、信頼性をさらに評価・改善できる。
parts.modelAnswer: The use of three repeats and a mean improves reliability compared with a single measurement. More repeats and a measure of spread, such as standard deviation or error bars, would allow the consistency of the results to be judged more clearly.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 3回の反復と平均値を使うことで、1回だけの測定より信頼性は高くなっています。さらに反復数を増やし、標準偏差やerror barなどのばらつきを示すと、結果の一貫性をより明確に評価できます。

subject: Biology SL
question: Answer all parts using the shared antibiotic-resistance data.

stimulus.title: Frequency of an antibiotic-resistance allele
stimulus.description: Two bacterial populations were started from the same large culture. One population was repeatedly exposed to antibiotic X; the control population was grown without the antibiotic.
stimulus.note: The resistance allele was present at low frequency before antibiotic exposure began.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Calculate the increase in resistance-allele frequency in the antibiotic-treated population from generation 0 to generation 20.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Compare the change in resistance-allele frequency in the antibiotic-treated and control populations.
markscheme: In the antibiotic-treated population, resistance frequency rises strongly from 0.06 to 0.89 over 20 generations.
In the control population, frequency remains low and fluctuates only slightly around the starting value, reaching 0.07 at generation 20.
markschemeJa: 抗生物質処理群では耐性対立遺伝子頻度が20世代で0.06から0.89へ大きく上昇する。
対照群では頻度は開始値付近の低い値にとどまり、小さく変動するだけで20世代目も0.07である。
parts.modelAnswer: The resistance allele rises from 0.06 to 0.89 with antibiotic exposure, whereas it remains close to its initial low frequency in the control population.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 抗生物質処理群では0.06から0.89へ大きく上昇しますが、対照群では開始時の低い頻度付近にほぼとどまります。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain how natural selection can account for the pattern in the antibiotic-treated population.
markscheme: Heritable variation was already present because some bacteria carried the resistance allele before treatment.
Antibiotic X acts as a selection pressure, so resistant bacteria survive and reproduce more successfully than susceptible bacteria.
Resistant bacteria therefore contribute a larger proportion of alleles to later generations, increasing resistance-allele frequency over time.
markschemeJa: 処理前から一部の細菌が耐性対立遺伝子をもっており、遺伝可能な変異がすでに存在していた。
抗生物質Xが選択圧となり、耐性細菌は感受性細菌より生存・繁殖しやすい。
そのため耐性細菌が後の世代へより多くの対立遺伝子を残し、耐性対立遺伝子頻度が時間とともに上昇する。
parts.modelAnswer: The population already contained heritable resistance variation. Antibiotic X selected against susceptible bacteria, while resistant bacteria survived and reproduced more successfully. They therefore contributed more copies of the resistance allele to later generations, causing its frequency to rise.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 集団には処理前から遺伝可能な耐性変異が存在していました。抗生物質Xの存在下では感受性細菌より耐性細菌が生き残り繁殖しやすいため、後の世代へ耐性対立遺伝子をより多く残し、その頻度が上昇します。

parts.label: (d)
parts.question: Explain why the data do not support the claim that antibiotic X caused bacteria to mutate because they needed resistance.
markscheme: The resistance allele was already present before antibiotic exposure, so the data support selection of pre-existing heritable variation rather than directed mutation in response to need.
markschemeJa: 耐性対立遺伝子は抗生物質曝露前から存在していたため、必要に応じた方向性のある突然変異ではなく、既存の遺伝的変異が選択されたことを支持する。
parts.modelAnswer: Resistance existed before treatment, so antibiotic X selected pre-existing variants rather than causing bacteria to mutate because they needed resistance.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 耐性は処理前から存在していたため、抗生物質Xが必要に応じた突然変異を起こしたのではなく、既存の耐性変異を選択したと考えられます。
